title: Eupen, the Capitol Theater and requisitioning a grand piano
summary: At the Eupen rest area he requisitions a collaborator's grand piano for Marian's show.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Then we went to, things were quiet there just before the Battle of the Bulge deal. So we left that area in the Ardennes Forest and went to a town called EUPEN. They pronounce it over there YOU-PEN. We pronounce it (OY-PEN). EUPEN. And they set us up in hotels and everything. And it was a rest area where the soldiers would come in from the front and get a hot bath and a whole new uniform and they could go around to the different Red Cross places and they lived in hotels. And their meals were free. Good home cooked meals from the Belgians. And you know, we gave jazz concerts.

And then we used to play in a theater, the Capitol Theater it was. And when we went to this theater we got it all set up for us to do our show; and terrible piano. The piano was absolutely, it was terrible. Marian, said, oh my God, she said I can't, what am I going to do? I can't play this thing. So we talked to Major Adams about it. He was the Special Service Officer and Major Adams says to me, he says, a little later he says, Jimmy, he says "I'll give you an order what we call a requisition order." He says, "there are a lot of, there were some

Nazi homes, collaborators and Nazis that were in town here and they have all the best stuff." And he said, "we have written down here what they have in their homes and everything and there's a place over here that has a brand new grand piano." You know, well these were the collaborators you know and they had all the best stuff.

So he gave me a requisition, he says, here's your requisition for a truck and eight men. So I took eight men, the truck and myself and a tommy gun (LAUGHTER) and went to the house and said here's a requisition you know. The man, the people, oh you can't do that. But the piano, oh, was beautiful, a beautiful piano.

Marian didn't know about this. Looked it over and we dismantled this thing and these people were screaming bloody murder you know. And who cared, collaborators? Get out of here! So I just kept going. I said, see the mayor, talk to the mayor you know. You'll get it back later. We're taking it to the Capitol Theater.
So we took it over and all. We moved the thing into the theater. Set it up and Marian came in for
rehearsal and here was the piano, that I had gotten for her. Well, she told.. .
That's like giving her a bouquet of flowers.
So she told me later on, she said that's when I decided to really pay attention to you, you know. You know, she liked me then.
